title: Bending Titanium Exhaust Tubing: Grade 2 vs 9, Mandrels & Purging
excerpt: Bending titanium exhaust tubing: grade 2 vs grade 9, why most builders buy pre-bent mandrel bends, springback test bends and back purging for welds.

notes: Direct page fetches were blocked in this environment, so every fact came from WebSearch result summaries of the listed pages. Please spot-check: (1) Smiths Metal: grade 9 density 4.48 g/cc (under 60% of steel) and 20-50% more strength than CP grades. (2) Aircraft Materials: grade 9 strength between grades 4 and 5; usable at higher temperatures than grades 1-4. (3) Bozeman Metal: welded thin-wall Ti exhaust tube in grades 1/2/9 to ASTM B862/B338; Bibus: grade 9 tube to AMS 4943/4944. (4) Rogue Fab titanium page: mandrel needed for thin wall, more springback than mild steel (depends on alloy/wall/CLR), galling, non-ferrous lube (Bend All 002 with bronze mandrels), annealed stock easier, mandrel nose just ahead of tangency, ~3.5 deg/s, under 4% deformation on 1.25 x .049 (3.5 in CLR) and 1.50 x .070; these are the maker's own tests. (5) Springback research: the yield/modulus-ratio statement came from a 2012 NWPU study on stress-relieved Ti-3Al-2.5V; the search summary did not make clear which NWPU URL holds that quote, so the linked NWPU page should be checked. Sheffield (White Rose) 2016 paper: wall thickness variation the largest contributor. (6) Postflow/cooling CONFLICT is stated in the text: Fabricator 'critical steps' (800 F, 20-25 s postflow, some codes below 500 F) vs 'only the clean survive' (500-800 F critical range) vs 'titanium you can weld it' (below ~500 F). (7) Weld color: Fabricator says any hint of blue suggests a shielding problem and 99.995% argon can leave some yellow-straw; gray/white unacceptable comes from a welding guide seen in search summary (source page not identified) and is stated generically; patent 7075033 (or the other titanium patent in the same search) said surface color is not always a reliable indicator - confirm which patent. (8) 'Some titanium welders use a trailing shield' is stated as practice without a specific source. (9) Product listings: Ticon B01FN3XTV0 says CP grade 1 but its material field also says 'Stainless Steel' (flagged in the article); TitanFlow B0F76Y97S3 listed as grade 1, 1.05D CLR; B00P2UB6QA brand not shown in search title (likely Ticon) so the article does not name a brand; Strictly Modified evidence URL is on us.amazon.com. (10) Purge volume example (3 in x 1 mm x 24 in = ~161 cu in, ~0.93 cu ft for 10 volumes) is our own arithmetic. No flow-rate recommendation is given because none could be sourced. Web search budget ran out during research.
